corrections.compiler_and_flags: clang -arch arm64 -O3 (generated/Makefile; NEON intrinsics in the generated code). The README does not say which build or machine produced the benchmark numbers.
corrections.caveats: CPU model, PyTorch version and thread count are not stated (generated/Makefile targets arm64 with clang -O3 and the README mentions a MacBook Air, so Apple Silicon is implied but not stated). Methodology is weak: validation/linear.py and validation/layer_normalization.py time a single cold first call of the PyTorch layer with time.time() (no warm-up), the generated C main() times one call with clock(), and 'average of five runs' means five such runs, so PyTorch's first-call overhead likely inflates the gap, especially for LayerNorm and GELU at [1,768]. The weights are synthetic patterns from the validation scripts (e.g. every Linear row is 0.1*(i+1)), not GPT-2 weights, and they are baked into the C source as constants. The README says baked layers with real GPT-2 weights could not be compiled on a MacBook Air, the MLP row has no Kaoken number, end-to-end model.generate() benchmarks were never done, and the headline still reads 'by X%'. About one month of commit history (Oct-Nov 2024, 17 commits); first-party.

corrections.caveats: Wins only at short sequences (N<=1024) and is 3-5% slower than cuDNN from N=2048 up. The Readme contradicts itself: the latency table gives K7/cuDNN 133.2% and 112.2% at N=512/1024 while the progression table gives 134.7% and 114.4% (and 99.8% vs 97.2% at N=2048); the NCU section says K7 'beats by ~35%' at N=1024 against 112.2% in the table; the progression legend says both 'lower = faster' and '>100% = faster' (the script computes 100*cuDNN/kernel, so higher is faster); and the torch.profiler line (0.003 ms for B=1 H=16 N=1024 D=128) is physically impossible on an RTX 5090, about 2,900 TFLOPS against a 419 TFLOPS peak (derived from page data). The 'NCU-equivalent' metrics come from an analytical script, not an Nsight Compute run. The baseline is PyTorch SDPA under sdpa_kernel(), timed per call including Python dispatch, and the script silently falls back to FLASH_ATTENTION or MATH if the cuDNN probe fails. CUDA, cuDNN and PyTorch versions and the host CPU are not stated. No license file, so the code must not be copied. First-party, 1 star, 59 commits, recent history from March 2026.
